s03_transmission.text: AI data center, interconnect and backbone network deployments drive rising incremental demand for optical fiber ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Demand reaches 577 million fiber-km in 2026 against constrained supply, producing a 180 million fiber-km shortfall with 92% utilization ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩
Supply-demand imbalance pushes finished fiber spot prices to 2.8-5x their 2025 levels, with BIF over 5x ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩
Higher fiber volumes and prices would benefit suppliers' revenue, but the article does not quantify any listed supplier's earnings impact

s04_key_evidence.label: supply shortage duration
s04_key_evidence.quote: substantial demand from AI data center-related applications has tightened global optical fiber supply since late 2025, with shortages expected to persist until at least 2028

s04_key_evidence.label: supply shortfall
s04_key_evidence.quote: this is expected to lead to a global supply shortfall of 180 million fiber-kilometers in 2026

s04_key_evidence.label: demand
s04_key_evidence.quote: Global optical fiber demand is estimated to reach 577 million fiber-kilometers in 2026

s04_key_evidence.label: capacity expansion lead time
s04_key_evidence.quote: expanding optical fiber preform capacity requires installing deposition equipment and establishing production processes, typically taking 18–24 months

s04_key_evidence.label: demand share
s04_key_evidence.quote: driven primarily by data center construction, which accounts for roughly 18–20% of the total

s04_key_evidence.label: spot price change
s04_key_evidence.quote: Tightening supply is projected to push spot prices for finished optical fiber products to 2.8–5 times their 2025 levels or higher

s04_key_evidence.label: inventory level
s04_key_evidence.quote: inventory levels have fallen from four months in 2024 to just one month

s04_key_evidence.label: price change
s04_key_evidence.quote: Prices for AI backbone fiber used in data center interconnects and high-capacity backbone networks are projected to reach approximately 2.8 times their 2025 levels

s04_key_evidence.label: price change
s04_key_evidence.quote: the average price of bend-insensitive fiber (BIF) used for cabling within data centers is expected to average more than five times its 2025 level in 2026

s04_key_evidence.label: demand share
s04_key_evidence.quote: That share is projected to rise to 30–35% in 2027

s04_key_evidence.label: price change
s04_key_evidence.quote: quotations for mainstream telecom fiber are expected to rise to around 3.7 times their previous levels

s04_key_evidence.label: capacity utilization
s04_key_evidence.quote: global optical fiber capacity utilization has climbed to 92% in 2026

s04_key_evidence.label: Some leading fiber suppliers are already booked into Q1 2027
s04_key_evidence.quote: Some leading suppliers are already booked into the first quarter of 2027

s04_key_evidence.label: contract volume
s04_key_evidence.quote: In September 2026, Verizon and Corning signed a multi-year supply agreement covering 129 million fiber-kilometers (approximately 80 million fiber-miles) of high-density optical fiber and connectivity solutions for delivery between 2027 and 2032

s06_why_now.catalyst_window: September 2026 Verizon-Corning multi-year supply agreement; supplier order books booked into Q1 2027 [MEASURED OBSERVATION]

near_term.text: Capacity utilization has climbed to 92% with inventories down to one month and some suppliers booked into the first quarter of 2027; tightening supply is projected to push spot prices to 2.8-5 times their 2025 levels. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩

structural.text: The shortage is driven by sustained AI data center demand and new preform capacity takes 18-24 months, so shortages are expected to persist until at least 2028.

s06_why_now.valuation_status: NOT_ASSESSED — the registry holds no consensus, market-expectation or valuation data; an opportunity here is not valuation proof

alternative_mechanisms.text: The article frames this shortage as different from past telecom infrastructure cycles, implicitly acknowledging prior fiber cycles have reversed; it does not rule out demand or capacity normalization.

disconfirming_observables.text: Fiber spot prices declining toward 2025 levels
Capacity utilization falling and inventories rebuilding above one month
New preform capacity coming online faster than the 18-24 month lead time
AI data center fiber demand growth slowing below forecast

unknowns.text: Whether named suppliers' (e.g. Corning) earnings or valuations already reflect the price surge
Whether the severalfold spot price increases translate to realized contract prices and margins given the shift to long-term agreements
Whether planned capacity expansions could close the shortfall faster than forecast

lower_priority_if.text: Major new preform capacity announced coming online before 2028
AI data center fiber demand forecasts cut

next_step.text: Check Corning's fiber segment revenue, pricing exposure and order backlog, and identify other listed optical fiber/preform producers to assess who benefits most from the shortage and whether valuations already price it in.

raise_priority_if.text: Additional large multi-year LTAs signed at elevated prices
Fiber spot prices continuing to rise into 2027
Suppliers raising capex guidance or backlog disclosures
